findings.claim: NetApp FY2026 10-K risk factors: competes with established public companies, newer flash-focused public companies and new entrants targeting the AI opportunity; markets have rapidly changing technology; AI technologies evolving with significant competition.

NetApp risk factor: business may be harmed if it cannot keep pace with rapid technological change or manage the transition from older products to new ones (10-K language surfaced in search; the exact filing year of the surfaced text is not confirmed).

Industry commentary lists newer approaches disrupting enterprise storage: hyperconverged storage, NVMe flash, container storage, composable/disaggregated infrastructure; Gartner-cited forecast that by 2028, 20% of I&O heads will deploy agentic-AI autonomous storage infrastructure, up from under 1% in 2026.
findings.source: Search results for 'enterprise storage alternative technology disruption 2026 2027' (Infinidat, TechTarget, DCD, others)

findings.claim: Roadmap commentary: enterprises continue to run production workloads on flash, object storage takes on broader scale-out/analytics role; DNA and optical ultra-cold archive media confined to narrow archival use cases.
findings.source: Intelligent CIO North America, Storage trends for 2026

substitute_technology.note: Search surfaced no named product that is stated to replace NetApp's core ONTAP/all-flash products. Excerpts left null because search returned summarized text, not verbatim snippets. as_of for Infinidat item is approximate (article dated 2026, exact day unknown).
